ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a triangle, with multiple lines parallel to the base drawn inside, dividing the triangle from the vertex to the base into 10 horizontal band-shaped regions. The gray regions are distributed alternately; counting downward from the vertex, the gray ones are the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th band-shaped regions, and the bottommost 10th band-shaped region is white. Reasoning: The problem states that these parallel lines divide each of the other two sides of the triangle into 10 equal parts. Therefore, the small triangle formed from the vertex to the kth division point is similar to the original triangle, with linear ratio k/10, and area ratio (k/10)^2 = k^2/100. Thus the area ratio of the kth band-shaped region from top to bottom is k^2/100 - (k-1)^2/100 = (k^2-(k-1)^2)/100. The gray bands correspond to k=1,3,5,7,9, so the gray area ratio is [1^2-0^2 + 3^2-2^2 + 5^2-4^2 + 7^2-6^2 + 9^2-8^2]/100 = (1+5+9+13+17)/100 = 45/100. Therefore the gray part accounts for 45% of the whole triangle.

raw_record.question_text: Lines drawn parallel to the base of the triangle pictured separate the other two sides into 10 equally large parts. What percentage of the triangle is grey?

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: the triangle is cut into 10 thin bands by lines parallel to the base, and the grey bands alternate; the grey set is the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th bands counting downward from the top tip, equivalently every other band with the bottom band white. From the text, the parallel lines divide the two slanted sides into 10 equal parts. Let the small similar triangle from the apex down to the kth division have linear scale k/10, so its area is k^2/100 of the whole triangle. Therefore the kth band from the top has area fraction (k^2-(k-1)^2)/100. Add the fractions for k=1,3,5,7,9: (1+5+9+13+17)/100=45/100, so the grey percentage is 45%.

method.method_draft: First inspect the picture and record the shading pattern: among the 10 parallel bands, the grey portions occupy alternating intervals along the altitude, namely the first, third, fifth, seventh, and ninth tenth-intervals measured from the apex. Use the text to know these intervals have equal side/altitude spacing because the sides are divided into 10 equal parts by lines parallel to the base. Apply an affine normalization: replace the triangle by any convenient triangle with height 10 and base width proportional to height; area ratios are unchanged. At height parameter t from the apex, the width is proportional to t, so the area density is proportional to t. The grey fraction is therefore the integral of 2t over t in [0,0.1] union [0.2,0.3] union [0.4,0.5] union [0.6,0.7] union [0.8,0.9], which equals the sum of endpoint-square differences: 0.01+(0.09-0.04)+(0.25-0.16)+(0.49-0.36)+(0.81-0.64)=0.45. Convert to 45%.
